headline: PORTAL uses shared feedback to choose test-time interventions and limit label queries
summary: Zhang, Wen, Li and Chen introduce PORTAL, a controller for choosing among fixed image-classification interventions, selecting inputs to label, and stopping when additional feedback cannot change the choice or its expected value is below its cost. The authors report results on PACS, CIFAR corruption benchmarks, ImageNet-C, and natural-domain vision-language settings. They report reduced class-block arrival harm on PACS and lower error on a 750,000-image ImageNet-C stream; when labels also train future PACS candidates, selected accuracy rises from 59.68% for fixed BN+flip to 72.64% for PORTAL. These are bounded preprint-reported results under the paper's data, candidate, query, and temporal assumptions; they have not been independently reproduced in this review.
